text:
$CRAWL is worth watching because the project is now advancing three things simultaneously

BXoHJddsWJLHtAopeiSbKUSELsu8hSFMs8baGMDkpump 

compute expansion, staking incentives, and training for the next-generation Queen model. These three updates correspond to the network’s data production capacity, the incentive mechanism for its token and NFTs, and the iteration of its core product.

However, the compute expansion figures are test results reported by the team, the staking data reflects participation interest, and Queen v5 is still an upcoming product milestone.

First, compute expansion directly impacts data production efficiency.

The team says Crawlnet has tripled its parallel crawler capacity, supporting up to 1,000 crawlers. In testing, the number of accepted pages read per minute increased by 4–5x. This means Queen could have access to a larger and fresher dataset for future training.

If these efficiency gains hold up in sustained operation, CRAWL’s core value would extend beyond simply training a crypto-focused AI model. It would be building a production pipeline that continuously collects industry data, trains models, and iterates on them.

Second, the staking system is beginning to test the community’s real commitment.

The team reported that approximately $205,000 in assets was staked within the first four hours of launch. This included 145 crawl.md NFTs, representing 15% of the collection, and 41.75 million CRAWL tokens, approximately 4.3% of the total supply. The initial staking period has a three-day lock, after which participants can unstake at any time and receive their assets and rewards.

More importantly, NFTs and tokens are now integrated into the same incentive mechanism, linking holders’ participation to the network ecosystem. However, short-term staking only demonstrates early participation interest. Whether it translates into long-term retention will depend on the source of rewards, continued participation rates, and what happens to capital after the lock expires.

Third, Queen v5 is the next key milestone to validate.

The ultimate value of compute expansion must be reflected in model iteration. Whether the new version can leverage a larger dataset and perform better on real-world tasks is the real test for this infrastructure upgrade.

For now, the team has announced that Queen v5 is about to begin training. Until training is completed, the model is released, and comparable performance results become available, this should not be treated as an achievement that has already been delivered.

My view is that CRAWL’s investment thesis is shifting from a simple bet on the AI + Crypto narrative toward a system in which community-operated crawlers continuously produce data, while compute infrastructure and model iteration advance together.

This has more potential than simply releasing an AI model because it attempts to connect data sourcing, training infrastructure, and community incentives into a closed loop. However, that loop still needs to be validated. These three updates alone are not enough to conclude that the business model is fully working.

The most important variable remains model quality. If Queen’s actual capabilities fail to improve alongside the expansion of data and compute, crawler counts, staking participation, and token incentives will struggle to support long-term value on their own.

I will be watching two things closely: the actual training results of Queen v5, and whether Crawlnet can consistently produce useful, unique, and verifiable data. These developments will determine whether the current infrastructure buildout can translate into genuine product competitiveness.

On the chart, I see the current price action as consolidation following a rally. The short-term structure remains bullish, but the token is approaching an important resistance zone. The expectation of a breakout alone is not enough to conclude that the rally will continue.

The biggest test now is whether CRAWL can break through the $5.8M–$6.0M market cap zone decisively. Rather than chasing the price higher, I would focus on two signals: a breakout above resistance supported by strong volume, or a pullback to the $4.6M–$4.8M area followed by clear buying support. Until one of these signals appears, waiting for confirmation is more prudent than declaring that a new leg up has already begun.

quoted_text:
$CRAWL market cap returning to $5M this time feels quite different from the first time it reached a $5M market cap.

BXoHJddsWJLHtAopeiSbKUSELsu8hSFMs8baGMDkpump 

The first time, the market was buying the story of “can a Crypto-native LLM actually be built?” Now, the market is starting to price in “it is actually being trained continuously, and the training system is scaling.”

The biggest change is that Queen has started evolving from a concept into a continuously iterated product.

When we first analyzed CRAWL, Queen v1 was still a newly launched experiment. Now it has moved into subsequent versions, with the model size, training data, and crawler network all continuing to grow. More importantly, the model is now public, and the training process is no longer just a one-time announcement. It is starting to form a cycle of crawler → data → training → model → next training.

So this rally is not simply because there is another new model. The market is starting to see that CRAWL is actually executing on its original thesis.

That’s why I think the direct catalysts for the market cap returning to $5M this time are mainly the launch of Queen v1, the rapid progress of subsequent versions, and renewed market attention.

The view expressed in the previous post also further strengthened this narrative: CRAWL could eventually evolve from a community-driven AI training experiment into infrastructure with specialized datasets, an open-source model, and an external developer ecosystem.

So what the market is betting on now is no longer just “can CRAWL build an AI model?”

The real bet is:Can CRAWL become a Crypto-native AI training network?

Queen is only the model itself. The potentially valuable part is the data production network being built around it. Crawlers continuously collect Crypto-native data, the data goes into datasets and is then used to train Queen, while creator fees can pay for the compute required for crawling and training.

If this cycle continues to expand, CRAWL may ultimately own not just a model, but an AI infrastructure stack of:Data Collection → Dataset → Training → Model → Developer Applications

So from a fundamental perspective, I think it is clearly stronger than it was the first time it reached $5M.

But one thing needs to be clear:Execution has strengthened, but Economic Value has not yet been proven.

We can already confirm that the crawlers, datasets, models, training, and compute are all progressing. But whether Queen actually has unique capabilities, whether external developers are willing to use it, and whether these product activities can ultimately generate real demand for CRAWL still needs to be validated.

What really matters next is not simply building an even larger Queen.

More importantly, can model capabilities make a meaningful leap, and can it attract real external usage?

If we eventually see a stronger Queen, a continuously expanding crawler network, external developers building products on top of Queen or its datasets, and eventually real users and token demand, then CRAWL’s valuation logic could shift from AI concept speculation toward Crypto-native AI infrastructure.

On the other hand, if it simply keeps adding crawlers, webpages, and training data without meaningfully improving Queen’s actual capabilities or attracting developers, then all that data ultimately remains just numbers on a dashboard.

So this is how I interpret the move from $1.7M → $5M:The first $5M was the market buying the future; the drop to $1.7M was expectations and attention fading; the return to $5M is happening because Queen has started producing continuously, and the market is willing to price the thesis again.

And how much further it can go from $5M will no longer depend on what the next announcement is, but on one thing:Can Queen prove that it is actually worth using by Crypto users?

If the answer starts becoming Yes, CRAWL’s valuation ceiling could open up significantly. If the answer remains No over the long term, then this rally is more likely to be a narrative re-rating rather than final confirmation of the fundamentals.

卧槽，程序员刚被 AI 抢饭碗，数学家的职业生涯也被 OpenAI 一夜清零了😲

纽约大学数学教授 Tristan Buckmaster 在采访中情绪激动地表示：

这批论文摧毁了年轻数学家的职业生涯。他甚至已经听说，至少 3 名研究者的整个研究计划被冲垮。

你可能不理解这有多残酷。

一个数学博士，可能花三五年攻克一道难题，毕业论文、科研经费、未来的教职，全指望这个研究方向。

结果睡一觉起来，OpenAI 把相关证明批量上传了，哪怕还需要验证，你辛辛苦苦准备发表的原创成果，可能已经失去了最重要的新颖性。

别人寒窗苦读几年，AI 一晚上批量出货，这谁受得了？

同时数据家Buckmaster 还揭露了另一个非常严重的问题：

你以为没用 AI，自己的研究思路就安全吗？

数学家申请科研经费，需要提前提交尚未公开的研究方案，而评审员可能直接把这些方案丢进大模型生成摘要。

现在数学圈的反应相当激烈。

剑桥、纽约大学等高校的研究者批评这批论文质量参差不齐，部分证明难以理解，独立验证还需要大量人力。

其中 3 篇已经因为符号错误被撤回。人类数学协会 AHM 更直接公开抵制，称一次释放 700 多份文件，是一次权力展示。连菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩的博客都转载了这份抵制声明。

程序员担心 AI 抢工作，数学家现在发现，AI 甚至可能在他们找到工作之前，就把用来申请工作的研究成果提前做完了。

quoted_text:
OpenAI 722 篇数学论文威力真猛，极端情况下公钥直接能推出私钥。

以太坊核心研究员发出警告：币圈该进入防御模式了😲😲😲（必看、必做）

卧槽，OpenAI 这次公开的数学仓库，影响可能远远超出 AI 圈。

以太坊基金会核心研究员 Justin Drake 直接向整个加密行业发出警告：

保护比特币、以太坊等加密资产的椭圆曲线密码学，可能在量子计算机成熟之前，就被 AI 找到破解方法。

他甚至提出了一种极端情况：最快几个月内，攻击者可能只需要大型 GPU 集群运行一周，就能从公钥反推出私钥。

我们一直以为，只要助记词不泄露、硬件钱包不被攻破，资产就安全了。

但如果 AI 找到了破解底层密码算法的数学捷径，黑客可能根本不需要碰你的设备，只要拿到已经暴露的公钥，就有机会算出私钥。

交易所冷钱包、巨鲸地址、机构托管，以及大量依赖椭圆曲线签名的链上基础设施，都可能面临风险。

所以 Drake 呼吁整个行业开始准备进入钱包防御模式，说白了，就是大户和机构先把大部分资产有序转移到公钥尚未暴露的新地址，尽量减少旧公钥暴露带来的风险。

以后每次签名，也考虑更换地址。

他还点名 Binance、Robinhood、Bitfinex、Tether 等机构，呼吁提前加强防护。

不过，不同链和地址类型的保护机制并不相同，这套办法也无法替代真正的抗攻击密码学升级。

这一切的导火索，就是 OpenAI 公开的 722 篇数学手稿。

它让 Drake 开始认真考虑一个过去看起来很遥远的风险：

AI 可能突然发现人类几十年都没有找到的数学捷径，让原本需要天文数字计算量的密码学难题，变得可以被普通计算集群攻破。

不过目前没有证据证明 ECDSA 已被攻破，Drake 所说的几个月也只是极端风险推演，大家千万不要恐慌性转账。

但我觉得，所有加密圈的人都应该认真看待这次警告。

以前大家担心量子计算机会不会攻破比特币，现在连 AI 都成了必须考虑的潜在威胁。

加密行业可能需要提前为一场尚未发生的密码学危机做准备了。

text:
两个财富自由的人，微博出来的 @indigox  和字节出来、提前退休的郭宇 @turingou  ，聊了一期：软件变得像牛奶一样便宜之后，我们到底还要交付什么。

1｜字节十年前就在跟黑箱共处
推荐算法工程师自己也说不清系统怎么运作，只能“通过实验来不断改进”。跟今天所有人用大模型一模一样。

抖音不是押出来的，是和火山小视频内部赛马四五年，靠“用户泛化”胜出。2019年拉一个新用户要50多元，郭宇当时判断：移动互联网这一轮结束了。

2｜AI没让工程师变轻松
一个人要扛工程师、架构师、设计师和产品经理的全部决策。郭宇自己花三四个月Vibe Coding了三十多个产品，很多没发布。身边很多人两三个月干完一两年的活，然后burnout。

AI替不了人做决策，因为它“没有主动的意图”。你要同时是工程师、架构师、设计师，最重要的是产品经理。你必须变成一个善于提问的人。

3｜App正在被Agent吃掉
“推荐引擎让内容千人千面，Agent让软件本身千人千面。”你的软件是你的软件，我的软件是我的软件。

用Claude Code、Codex搭一个CRM是“两分钟、五分钟、十分钟的事”。做好软件放进应用市场分发，“已经有点失去意义了”。

Meta新出的Muse，自动打电话订餐厅、出国旅行预订、管理信息。它“不需要一个单独的App”，直接集成在Instagram、WhatsApp、Messenger里。过去你要用一堆软件拼出一条工作流，现在不需要工作流了。

郭宇自己就被这样“吃掉”过：今年三四月做的一个替人打电话的产品，不少葡语、西语用户在用。到了快十月，超级应用已经把这些功能内置了，专门做某一件事的小软件，单独分发已没必要。

4｜Agent OS：未来的算力租用
已经有人把Agent而不是App当作Linux的一等公民，OpenAI买了大量Mac mini训练模型操作Mac。五年尺度，租用的算力都会变成“Virtual Agent Server”。

但郭宇也提醒了一个暗面：如果所有人都通过Agent管理电脑，中心化的Agent通道本身就会成为一个巨大的安全单点。“如果OpenAI被攻击了，或者它的连接被劫持了，其实就变成世界上最大的肉鸡集群。”

5｜只有2%到3%的人能成为Pro User
一个人“相当于过去五六十人的公司”。AI对社会和商业的影响“可能只完成了2%、3%”。

AI是一张白纸，只放大有想法的人。大多数人上班领导派活、干完走人、回家躺着看电视，没有想法，也没想过怎么提需求。所以AI呈现出明显的两极：对Pro User，它是十倍放大器；对大多数人，它只是更方便的搜索引擎。

6｜真人本身成为最稀缺的差异化
“Software is media, everything is media。”抖音字幕故意写错别字，完播率大幅提高。这个技巧很快被识别并屏蔽，但工程师永远不知道创作者下一次会怎么Hack。

text:
美国有个音乐人，给自己养了 1 万个机器人听众，硬是从 Spotify 等音乐平台薅走了 800 多万美元。

这个叫 Michael Smith 的哥们，刚被美国法院判了 18 个月监禁。

从 2017 年开始，他就在各大音乐平台上批量注册虚假账户，让机器人全天候循环播放自己上传的歌曲。后来发现音乐不够用，干脆找来一家 AI 音乐公司，批量生产了几十万首歌，再给它们编造各种歌名和艺人身份。

最离谱的数据出现在 2023 年 4 月。在 YouTube Music 的家庭套餐播放渠道，他的机器人一个月刷出了 8090 万次播放。同期 Taylor Swift 的全部歌曲在这个渠道加起来只有 930 万次。

而且这哥们还挺懂风控。

他知道一首歌突然播放十亿次肯定会被发现，于是故意把流量分散到成千上万首 AI 歌曲上。早在 2018 年，他就在邮件里催促合作伙伴赶紧生产海量歌曲，好绕过平台的反作弊机制。

我觉得这个案子最值得关注的地方，是它暴露了 AI 内容经济一个相当荒诞的漏洞。

AI 负责生产内容，Bot 负责制造消费，平台按照播放数据支付真金白银。整个过程中甚至不需要有一个真实的听众。

更糟糕的是，音乐平台的版税来自共享收入池。机器人每刷出一笔虚假收入，真实音乐人能够分到的钱就少了一部分。

过去我们总担心 AI 生成的垃圾内容太多，没人愿意看。现在发现，根本不需要有人看，只要平台愿意为流量付钱，就有人有动力把生产和消费一起自动化。

这套逻辑显然也不只适用于音乐行业。

当内容和流量都可以由机器批量制造，互联网过去二十年建立起来的那套以点击、播放和互动衡量价值的商业模式，恐怕要重新算账了。

世界杯后，头部预测市场发展方向已然逐渐分化

Kalshi 巩固 off-chain、合规和体育偏科优势，并向 Perp DEX 永续扩展

Polymarket 发力 US 站和 Perp DEX 永续，对于 Web3 社区反馈和关注却有所降低

Predict Fun 专注 Crypto 以及股票短时涨跌市场，并为 CEX 事件合约提供支持

text:
There’s currently some FUD about @Backpack, subtly implying that the exchange is still young (only 4 years old) and that withdrawing $10K gets delayed for 4 hours.

I want to clarify: This is an optional security feature, not a bug or “stuck funds.”

Backpack has a Withdrawal Delay feature:
Go to Settings → Accounts: Exchange → Security → Withdrawal Delay. 

Users can turn it on themselves and choose the waiting time (e.g. 4h, 12h, 24h, etc.).

It only applies when withdrawing to a new external wallet address (not yet saved in the Address Book, or saved for less time than the delay you’ve set).

Addresses that have been whitelisted / saved longer than the delay period are withdrawn normally and quickly.

Internal transfers between sub-accounts are not affected by the delay.

Armani even actively recommends using this feature, going as far as saying that “instant withdrawals are an utterly stupid thing that crypto has normalized,” because it helps protect against hacks, clipboard malware, mistyped addresses, etc.

A guy who left over $4M on the Fomo app got hacked. Today, $80M stored on Ledger was completely drained due to a supply chain issue.

Yet when Backpack is trying to protect its users, some people use that as a reason to criticize it?

text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

quoted_text:
papertrade launch timing and details

papertrade is expected to launch at 14:00 UTC on 10.10.2026, following the scheduled hyperevm network upgrade. 

at this time trading through the frontend will be enabled.

deposits will pause for a short period of time at 13:45 UTC, fifteen minutes before, to ensure that trading has the utmost priority during launch. if you wish to participate in the launch you must predeposit.

launch congestion

papertrade will be congested at the start due to launch demand. expect temporarily long confirmation wait times, especially for smaller notional trades. 

the frontend relayer plays an important role during launch, controlling how transactions are submitted to the hyperevm. some actions like staking distributions run separately in big blocks. the chain will always look as if only half of all possible gas is being used, this is optimal. using more than this would exponentially raise fees within minutes to unpayable prices.

oi limits

papertrade has individual atomic position limits of 10m. there is no limit on the number of 10m positions a user can have. papertrade also has floating oi headroom per market/side, which determines how much oi can be opened in a very short period. these are not designed to be triggered through normal trading usage and are set at 1bn per market/side for launch.

asym pnl fee parameters

papertrade inherits rollbit’s asymmetric fee pnl curve 

the parameters are:
-baseRate: .1
-rateMultiplier: 15000
-rateExponent: 1
-referenceNotional: 100000*k (k=1m)
-positionMultiplier: 814.598 btc / 483.979 eth
-profit deadman: 0.2 basis points

a visualization of the pnl parameter curve is below

admin keys

the papertrade admins (2 of 3 multisigs consisting of @izebel_eth @blurr @UngusTrade ) perform three separate roles: 

-guardian: pause opens and freeze individual/global markets. if a market is frozen any existing positions can still be closed against the paused bbo mid.

-owner: set impact curve and fee parameters. change configure relayers/keepers. list new markets and upgrade the contracts. all contract upgrades are gated by a 7 day timelock.

-markets: adjust the oi headroom per market/side. set the minimum margin and minimum position sizes.

read more about these features at: https://t.co/TTCuHgCHpB

text:
孙正义可能想出了一个给 AI 创造收入的办法，直接把 AI 未来的客户也买下来。

《金融时报》刚刚报道，软银正在找中东投资人筹集最多 1000 亿美元，已经和阿联酋等海湾国家的潜在出资方展开初步谈判。

孙正义打算成立一只新的收购基金，直接买下现有企业，再通过 AI、机器人和自动化技术改造它们的运营。软银自己的机器人业务 Roze 也可能参与其中。

这让我想起 2017 年，孙正义同样从中东筹集巨额资金，搞出了规模近 1000 亿美元的愿景基金。当时他想用资本押中下一代互联网巨头，结果既投出了字节跳动这样的赢家，也在 WeWork 身上栽了大跟头。

九年过去，孙正义的胃口一点没变，玩法却有了很大变化。

根据软银 10 月 1 日的公告，它已经累计向 OpenAI 投资 646 亿美元，持有约 13% 的股份。假设 OpenAI 未来估值达到 2 万亿美元，这部分股权的账面价值就有 2600 亿美元。

但我觉得更有意思的是，孙正义现在似乎已经不满足于押注 AI 技术本身了。

如果这只基金真的成立，软银一边持有 OpenAI 这样的大模型公司，一边控制大量传统企业，甚至可以通过自己的机器人业务参与改造。这意味着它有机会同时影响 AI 的供给和需求。

而且这笔钱还可以由外部投资人来出。

这个思路其实挺符合孙正义一贯的风格。他习惯先相信一个足够大的未来，再调动远超自身资产负债表承受能力的资本去实现它。

但风险也非常明显。软银刚刚为了投资 OpenAI 发行了 111 亿美元高收益债券，如今又要启动千亿美元级别的收购计划。AI 在真实企业里究竟能创造多少可以兑现的利润，现在还没有足够的证据。

如果这套模式跑通，孙正义可能会成为 AI 改造传统产业过程中最大的资本受益者之一。

如果跑不通，那就是当年愿景基金的故事，在一个贵得多的估值体系里重新上演。

I'll preface this by saying HYPE is the best project in the space at the moment; but let's take a more objective look at some of the not so great components of Hyperliquid:

-HyperEVM is by in large, a failure in its current state. Almost no projects have gotten any real traction; and those that have, are basically just extraction vehicles and or have down dodgy things to extract in roundabout ways.
-HIP-4 has failed to gain traction; and it has failed to be a significant competitor towards Polymarket or Kalshi thus far. 
-Every single NFT collection is a failure outside of Hypurr's; which themselves are down 80-90% from the peak and have only retained some value in hopes of a future airdrop for holders.
-Large concentration of supply with little to no clarity on airdrops or another points season; or anything of the sort. 
-Not a fan of the large OTC sales out of the blue to some unnamed entity(s). Backroom deals to large players goes against the HL ethos. These are large sales. Not a great sign of confidence at the current price levels tbh. (re; SOL and BTC DAT's buying at/near the high's.) 
 -Community has be left hung out to dry since the TGE airdrop (which was great, but that was almost 2 years ago.) No airdrops, no incentives, no points seasons, nothing. Radio silence outside of a "thank you" at the event and a continued hope for some random retroactive airdrop at some point, eventually, maybe, potentially. 
-Community loyalty has a time decay. If users do not feel respected for their loyalty, they will move somewhere else (already seeing this to some degree with @variational_io ) Financial incentives have to be there; it's just the way it is. Don't have to look far to see what happens when incentives, interest, and liquidity dry up (ETH, SOL.)

I worry Hyperliquid has gotten complacent being the top dog and they've lost the plot a bit. Competition is only going to get stronger. Community/users will begin to depart if they are not incentivized to stay which would then put downward pressure on HL metrics.

quoted_text:
papertrade launch timing and details

papertrade is expected to launch at 14:00 UTC on 10.10.2026, following the scheduled hyperevm network upgrade. 

at this time trading through the frontend will be enabled.

deposits will pause for a short period of time at 13:45 UTC, fifteen minutes before, to ensure that trading has the utmost priority during launch. if you wish to participate in the launch you must predeposit.

launch congestion

papertrade will be congested at the start due to launch demand. expect temporarily long confirmation wait times, especially for smaller notional trades. 

the frontend relayer plays an important role during launch, controlling how transactions are submitted to the hyperevm. some actions like staking distributions run separately in big blocks. the chain will always look as if only half of all possible gas is being used, this is optimal. using more than this would exponentially raise fees within minutes to unpayable prices.

oi limits

papertrade has individual atomic position limits of 10m. there is no limit on the number of 10m positions a user can have. papertrade also has floating oi headroom per market/side, which determines how much oi can be opened in a very short period. these are not designed to be triggered through normal trading usage and are set at 1bn per market/side for launch.

asym pnl fee parameters

papertrade inherits rollbit’s asymmetric fee pnl curve 

the parameters are:
-baseRate: .1
-rateMultiplier: 15000
-rateExponent: 1
-referenceNotional: 100000*k (k=1m)
-positionMultiplier: 814.598 btc / 483.979 eth
-profit deadman: 0.2 basis points

a visualization of the pnl parameter curve is below

admin keys

the papertrade admins (2 of 3 multisigs consisting of @izebel_eth @blurr @UngusTrade ) perform three separate roles: 

-guardian: pause opens and freeze individual/global markets. if a market is frozen any existing positions can still be closed against the paused bbo mid.

-owner: set impact curve and fee parameters. change configure relayers/keepers. list new markets and upgrade the contracts. all contract upgrades are gated by a 7 day timelock.

-markets: adjust the oi headroom per market/side. set the minimum margin and minimum position sizes.

read more about these features at: https://t.co/TTCuHgCHpB

text:
how to not get your crypto hacked.

bookmark this forever:

1. hardware
- buy direct from the company or an authorized retailer. never random resellers
- seed card already filled in when you received = scam. throw it
- ship it to a pickup point, not your home
- update firmware only through the official app

2. seed
- metal over paper. never a photo, cloud or notes app
- never enter your seed into a website or software wallet. restore only through your hardware wallet's official recovery
- don't split your seed manually. no redundancy and it leaks information. use shamir or multisig instead
- test your backup before funding: built-in check or wipe and restore. untested backup = no backup
- two copies, two locations. fire is a hacker too if seed burns

3. setup
- vault: a hardware wallet that never touches dapps
- hot wallet for daily use. burner for anything new
- bigger bags: passphrase on top. small decoy bag on the seed, real bag behind the passphrase
- back up the passphrase too, stored apart from the seed. lose it and nothing recovers your coins
- multisig when the amount justifies it. no single point of failure

4. signing (where most people get drained)
- verify on the device, never trust the website alone. bybit lost $1.5B to a compromised UI
- can't read it? don't sign it
- "free" signatures can drain you with zero gas (permits)
- one malicious eip-7702 authorization can delegate control of your entire account
- on solana, one bad tx can reassign your token accounts. simulate before you sign
- review approvals monthly. revoke what you don't need

5. sending
- never copy addresses from tx history. scammers plant lookalikes
- check the full address on the device, not just the first and last 4
- small test tx before every big one

6. machine
- a laptop that only touches crypto. clean browser, no random extensions
- download wallets only from the official site. app stores and search results are full of fakes
- never run "meeting apps", game builds or files strangers send
- never share your screen or install remote access. "support" asking for anydesk = scam
- bookmark every site. never click search ads
- surprise airdrops and NFTs = trap

7. exchanges
- unique password everywhere. 1password or bitwarden
- 2FA with an authenticator app or passkey. never SMS
- 2FA backup codes offline. not in email, not in cloud
- lock your SIM with a carrier PIN. sim swaps still work
- separate email only for crypto. nobody knows it
- turn on withdrawal whitelists
- not your keys, not your coins. move out what you're not trading

8. opsec
- don't flex your bags or your setup. wrench attacks are rising
- support never DMs first.
- avoid phishing emails, only trust official sources
- have an inheritance plan. dead keys are lost coins

9. quantum (check my other quantum tweet for detailed advice)
- not a threat today and anyone selling quantum panic is selling something
- btc: never reuse addresses. sending from one exposes its public key forever
- btc: park long-term coins in addresses that have never sent a tx. taproot (bc1p) and old p2pk show the key from day one
- btc: bip-360 proposes a step toward quantum-resistant addresses. not live. proposals also exist to freeze unmigrated coins
- eth + erc20: sending a tx exposes your public key. signing messages can expose it too so keep major bag on clean wallet
- sol: your address is your public key. exposed from day one. experimental winternitz vaults exist, not standard wallet protection

hardware rarely gets hacked. people do.

🔐 For years, Galactica has been building privacy infrastructure, with a particular focus on private identity: enabling users to prove required facts without revealing the underlying personal data.

🤖 The rise of autonomous AI agents has made this work even more relevant. As agents begin to access services, select models, make payments and complete transactions on behalf of people and organizations, they need privacy-preserving ways to demonstrate authorization, eligibility and payment.

🤝 Together with our partners at @aztecnetwork , we identified delegated KYC for AI agents as a particularly important application of our zkKYC primitives. A user should be able to grant an agent a limited, verifiable credential; the agent should be able to prove eligibility without exposing the underlying identity documents; and the resulting payment should not create a public trail that makes the user's activity easy to reconstruct.

🧮 But identity is only one part of the problem. The emergence of AI has created an entirely new range of applications for modern cryptography, particularly around inference the process at the core of every AI system and, increasingly, everyday digital services. Our work has therefore expanded from private identity to private settlement and private inference.

🎯 This leads to our broader mission: bringing privacy to the entire AI inference value chain.

🧠 Private identity protects the party behind a request and allows users or agents to prove only the facts required for access. Private settlement prevents payment activity from becoming a public record of user behavior. Private inference protects prompts, context and outputs during computation.

🙈 These layers cannot be treated as separate privacy problems. A hidden prompt is not truly private if identity, payment history, model selection or usage patterns can still reveal the user's intent. Our goal is to connect identity, settlement and inference into a single system in which every stage discloses only the minimum information necessary.

🚀 This is what we are excited to build with Aztec and other partners. As AI becomes an execution layer for everyday life, privacy must become a native property of its infrastructure not an optional feature added afterward.

🌐 By combining zero-knowledge identity, private settlement and confidential inference, we have an opportunity to build an AI economy in which both people and autonomous agents can prove, pay and compute without surrendering unnecessary information.

Our new website: https://t.co/X6N1ky6L6D

微软发布 Microsoft-Decision-1：专做“选择题”的 AI 模型，基于 Qwen3.5-9B 后训练

微软推出新模型 Microsoft-Decision-1。它不写文章也不聊天，只做一件事：给定几个选项，快速判断该选哪个，并给每个选项打一个概率分。Satya Nadella 在 X 上宣布了这个模型，它已在微软的 AI 开发平台 Microsoft Foundry 上线，之后还会上 OpenRouter（一个聚合多家模型的 API 平台）。

微软把这类模型叫“决策模型”。大语言模型擅长生成文字、推理复杂问题，但软件里很多 AI 调用其实只是在做判断：这条用户反馈属于哪一类？这个请求该交给哪个模型处理？智能体下一步该继续、重试，还是交给人？这类问题的答案都在固定选项里，拿大模型来答又慢又贵。决策模型直接输出结构化结果，程序拿到就能用。

它是在阿里开源模型 Qwen3.5-9B 的基础上后训练出来的，只算一遍就出结果。支持是/否题、多选题和打分，也能按评分标准给 AI 的回答或智能体的动作打分。微软说之后会换到自家 MAI 模型和 OpenAI 的模型上重新训练。

它输出的概率是“校准过”的：模型说有 90% 把握时，实际大约十次能对九次。开发者可以据此设门槛，把握高就自动执行，把握低就转人工审核。

以下性能数据都来自微软自己的测试。在 36 个基准、近 15 万道题的对比里，它的准确率最高。速度上，它比第二名 Quyet-1.0-Large 快 4.5 倍，比 GPT-6 Sol 快约 35 倍。微软还测了稳定性：把同一个请求换种说法、打乱选项顺序等，一共八种改动，判断结果平均只有 1.3% 会变，打乱选项顺序时一次都没变。

速度之所以重要，是因为智能体干活经常要连着做几十个小判断。每个判断慢 100 毫秒，20 步下来就要多等 2 秒。

微软内部已经在用。Xbox 研究团队用它把 1 万多条玩家反馈和评论按主题归类，质量和 GPT-6 Sol 相当，速度快 14 倍以上，成本低 200 倍。Copilot 团队用它给回答质量打分，效果接近 GPT5.6 Luna，速度快 100 倍。

对开发者来说，它适合那些答案在有限选项里的环节，比如模型路由、意图识别、内容审核、数据打标签、给 AI 输出当评委，以及让 AI 操作电脑时选下一步点哪里。把这些环节从大模型换成它，延迟和账单都能降下来。

价格是每百万输入 Token 0.042 美元，输出免费。现在就可以在 Microsoft Foundry 的模型目录里调用。

text:
NEAR Intents got called centralized for a week because it refuses to trade hacked funds. Here is what the biggest L2 on Ethereum did in April:

> KelpDAO got drained on April 18: 116,500 rsETH, $292M. Investigators pointed at North Korea. Part of the money sat on Arbitrum.

> On April 21 Arbitrum's Security Council, 9 of 12 signers, upgraded the chain's inbox contract on Ethereum to add one function: send a transaction as any address. They used it to send a transaction as the exploiter, moving about $71M in ETH to an address with no owner. Then they reverted the contract.

> No issuer blacklist, no sequencer trick. The chain impersonated a user and emptied his wallet at the protocol layer. The council had never used its powers this way before.

> ArbitrumDAO voted to move the ETH to a recovery multisig. A week later a US court froze it in a lawsuit against North Korea, and the money is still tied up in that.

> Offchain Labs' CEO: We're no more or less decentralized today than we were yesterday.

I think they did the right thing. Same as I think about Intents. But look at the two mechanisms. On Arbitrum nine people signed a chain upgrade that acted in the thief's name, once, after the fact. On Intents an automated system scores every trade for stolen funds before it executes, and a human council only reviews what got caught mid-flight. Nobody is rewriting anybody's balance. NEAR Intents is just getting better at detecting threats, and the detection is a program in a hardware enclave, not a committee.

quoted_text:
papertrade launch timing and details

papertrade is expected to launch at 14:00 UTC on 10.10.2026, following the scheduled hyperevm network upgrade. 

at this time trading through the frontend will be enabled.

deposits will pause for a short period of time at 13:45 UTC, fifteen minutes before, to ensure that trading has the utmost priority during launch. if you wish to participate in the launch you must predeposit.

launch congestion

papertrade will be congested at the start due to launch demand. expect temporarily long confirmation wait times, especially for smaller notional trades. 

the frontend relayer plays an important role during launch, controlling how transactions are submitted to the hyperevm. some actions like staking distributions run separately in big blocks. the chain will always look as if only half of all possible gas is being used, this is optimal. using more than this would exponentially raise fees within minutes to unpayable prices.

oi limits

papertrade has individual atomic position limits of 10m. there is no limit on the number of 10m positions a user can have. papertrade also has floating oi headroom per market/side, which determines how much oi can be opened in a very short period. these are not designed to be triggered through normal trading usage and are set at 1bn per market/side for launch.

asym pnl fee parameters

papertrade inherits rollbit’s asymmetric fee pnl curve 

the parameters are:
-baseRate: .1
-rateMultiplier: 15000
-rateExponent: 1
-referenceNotional: 100000*k (k=1m)
-positionMultiplier: 814.598 btc / 483.979 eth
-profit deadman: 0.2 basis points

a visualization of the pnl parameter curve is below

admin keys

the papertrade admins (2 of 3 multisigs consisting of @izebel_eth @blurr @UngusTrade ) perform three separate roles: 

-guardian: pause opens and freeze individual/global markets. if a market is frozen any existing positions can still be closed against the paused bbo mid.

-owner: set impact curve and fee parameters. change configure relayers/keepers. list new markets and upgrade the contracts. all contract upgrades are gated by a 7 day timelock.

-markets: adjust the oi headroom per market/side. set the minimum margin and minimum position sizes.

read more about these features at: https://t.co/TTCuHgCHpB

Thanks to everyone who joined us at @Vault__Summit Singapore!

We keep getting asked why Morpho hosts a Vault Summit when we say our focus is primarily credit markets, not vaults. 

TLDR: If Vaults win, Onchain Credit wins.

Bringing $200T of global credit onchain will take millions of credit markets, enough to serve every risk profile and every financing need. Thousands already run on Morpho, and they’re getting more sophisticated, like Morpho Midnight markets. 

Vaults are how a lot of that liquidity is coordinated and reaches markets in an efficient way. 

We built Morpho Vaults as open source so the curators a distributors ecosystem could grow.

We think onchain vaults and curation will become one of the biggest categories in the industry, and it deserves its own stage. Hence Vault Summit. See you at the next one!

papertrade launch timing and details

papertrade is expected to launch at 14:00 UTC on 10.10.2026, following the scheduled hyperevm network upgrade. 

at this time trading through the frontend will be enabled.

deposits will pause for a short period of time at 13:45 UTC, fifteen minutes before, to ensure that trading has the utmost priority during launch. if you wish to participate in the launch you must predeposit.

launch congestion

papertrade will be congested at the start due to launch demand. expect temporarily long confirmation wait times, especially for smaller notional trades. 

the frontend relayer plays an important role during launch, controlling how transactions are submitted to the hyperevm. some actions like staking distributions run separately in big blocks. the chain will always look as if only half of all possible gas is being used, this is optimal. using more than this would exponentially raise fees within minutes to unpayable prices.

oi limits

papertrade has individual atomic position limits of 10m. there is no limit on the number of 10m positions a user can have. papertrade also has floating oi headroom per market/side, which determines how much oi can be opened in a very short period. these are not designed to be triggered through normal trading usage and are set at 1bn per market/side for launch.

asym pnl fee parameters

papertrade inherits rollbit’s asymmetric fee pnl curve 

the parameters are:
-baseRate: .1
-rateMultiplier: 15000
-rateExponent: 1
-referenceNotional: 100000*k (k=1m)
-positionMultiplier: 814.598 btc / 483.979 eth
-profit deadman: 0.2 basis points

a visualization of the pnl parameter curve is below

admin keys

the papertrade admins (2 of 3 multisigs consisting of @izebel_eth @blurr @UngusTrade ) perform three separate roles: 

-guardian: pause opens and freeze individual/global markets. if a market is frozen any existing positions can still be closed against the paused bbo mid.

-owner: set impact curve and fee parameters. change configure relayers/keepers. list new markets and upgrade the contracts. all contract upgrades are gated by a 7 day timelock.

-markets: adjust the oi headroom per market/side. set the minimum margin and minimum position sizes.

read more about these features at: https://t.co/TTCuHgCHpB

Explaining the haze situation gripping Southeast Asia

1. The haze is caused by fires, mainly in southern parts of the Indonesian islands of Sumatra and Kalimantan (Borneo).

2. The fires happen for of a mix of reasons: lightning strikes, accidents, and farmers starting them deliberately to clear the land.

3. The fires are not forest fires. They’re peat fires. Peat is swampy land full of dead plants. When it burns it burns dirtier than wood; it’s worse for your health.

4. Normally the peat fires are put out fast by rain. It’s not happening this year because of the super El Niño which happens every 10-20 years. Long story short is that it’s causing there to be no rain.

5. Compounding on this lack of rain is decades of palm oil and paper pulp cultivation which has dried out the flammable peat. The prime beneficiary is a corporation that was founded by a multidecibillionaire Chinese immigrant to Indonesia who, without converting to Islam, had at least 8 wives and 40+ children.

6. The last time the haze was this bad was late 1997 early 1998. It caused bad rice harvests and contributed to the Asian financial crisis which featured currency collapses and widespread rioting.

7. It’s unclear whether or not the haze can be alleviated by the techniques used by Dubai for rain and China to clear their air before big events (increasingly less necessary as they improved their air generally over last 10 years).

8. Unfortunately the haze is expected to last until at least November if not December, when the rains should return. Depending on how strong and long the rainy season is, the peat fires may not be permanently put out and may last, in a more subdued way, until heavier rains of April.

{

~/.claude/agents/scout.md

---
name: scout

tools: Read, Grep, Glob

name: critic

model: opus

text:
An AI model sent an invented homicide tip to a real police department when it was only supposed to be generating practice examples.

Anthropic disclosed the case on Friday, in a report on unintended actions by Claude during testing and internal use.

The tip went through a Philadelphia police form, was flagged as spam and was never forwarded to investigators.

In another case, Claude Mythos Preview found an injection flaw on a university server and used it to run commands after a research tool it needed returned an error.

In a third, Claude Mythos 5 avoided a state agency's data fee by requesting the free access token that the agency's public dashboard hands to every visitor.

Anthropic calls most of this persistence, meaning the model works around a restriction instead of stopping when a task cannot be completed as given.

It says the real-world impact was minimal, but it has cut live internet access from all internal evaluations until its monitoring reliably catches these behaviours.

For onchain agents, a failed swap or a blocked call should end in a clean stop, not an invitation to find another route.

text:
What sets the price of a Nvidia token at 3am on a Sunday? Cantex opened trading on 7 Oct in NVDAe and SPCXe, two tokens @edeldotfinance issued on @CantonNetwork, linked to Nvidia and SpaceX, according to posts from both companies that CantonNews reported on 8 Oct. Cantex says they trade outside regular US market hours. It's still invite-only. Edel says its earlier pair, SPYe and QQQe, passed $2 million in combined on-chain volume on 1 Oct.

When Nasdaq is closed, the token can't follow Nvidia's price, because there isn't a new one. The Cantex order book sets it alone. What pulls it back to the stock on Monday is whoever can redeem or hedge at the open, and the coverage doesn't say who can redeem these two.

I'd bet less on the after-hours trading mattering than on that redemption line. Weekend access only helps if the gap closes when the market reopens.

If you're trading these, a weekend quote is a guess about Monday, and $2 million of volume across a month is a thin book that one order can move. Someone running a market-making desk sees the same hours as a hedging problem. You're quoting a stock you can't trade, so the spread has to carry the weekend.

The counter is that Edel and Cantex may publish redemption terms for these two, and that would answer most of this.

Open all weekend means priced all weekend, by someone.

I hold $CC, $CNTN and $EDEL.

Who can redeem NVDAe at the Monday open?

A 3-day TikTok warm-up can save you from months of dead reach.

*Day 1*
•⁠  ⁠Create the account  
•⁠  ⁠Don’t post  
•⁠  ⁠Don’t add a bio link  
•⁠  ⁠Scroll your niche FYP for 30 minutes  
•⁠  ⁠Like 15–20 videos  
•⁠  ⁠Leave 5–7 real comments  
•⁠  ⁠Follow 8–10 relevant accounts  

*Day 2*
Repeat the process.

Also search your niche keywords and watch 10+ videos to completion so TikTok learns what the account is about.

Still no posting.

*Day 3*
Post one non-promotional slideshow:

•⁠  ⁠Pure value  
•⁠  ⁠Relevant trending sound  
•⁠  ⁠Unique images  
•⁠  ⁠No hard sell  

Wait 24 hours.

If the post gets traction, start posting consistently and add your funnel.

If it completely dies, reassess the content and account setup before scaling.

Patience early beats forcing content into a cold account.

quoted_text:
You know what's funny about this?

Three Sentora team members told me this post is wrong and that I should do better research since I published it.

Sentora is the curator behind the markets I covered that rely on market price oracles.

So I asked their team a simple question: what would happen if USDe suddenly drops to $0.85 on DEXs and stays at that price for an hour tomorrow? (without USDe losing any of its backing)

None of them wanted to directly answer, so I'll give you the answer: 

Highly leveraged loopers in the USDe markets curated by Sentora would be liquidated in a scenario like this, even if USDe remains fully backed. 

Is USDe dropping to $0.85 on DEXs a likely scenario? Definitely not. But even a 5x smaller temporary depeg could be very bad for highly leveraged loopers. 

Depegs like this can happen even if USDe works completely fine. They can happen to any stablecoin, not just USDe.

Even USDC depegged in March 2023 to $0.88.

I have nothing against Sentora, and my goal in these posts wasn't to attack them in any way.  

I actually used many markets curated by Sentora in the past and will continue using the ones which I believe are set up in the right way.

The only reason I mentioned its sUSDe and USDe markets is to make borrowers aware of the risks involved, since I know that very few people know how to research oracles.  

Instead of telling me my research is wrong when that's not true, I'd much rather see Sentora acknowledge the issue and ensure its future markets are designed to better protect borrowers. 

I wish them well!

text:
$BORDR recent rally is not about an ordinary Meme. 

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

The market is betting on a customizable Token Standard on Solana, along with the DEX, launchpad, and developer ecosystem being built around it.

I believe the key catalyst behind the recent move is that the project is transitioning from simply pitching a new token standard to gradually launching product modules, opening up developer tools, and expanding external trading access. However, we need to distinguish between improving product development and proven ecosystem demand. The former is becoming more evident; the latter remains unproven.

First, Bordrless has a differentiated technical narrative. It is not simply copying Uniswap V4 Hooks. Instead, it extends programmable rules from the liquidity pool layer to the token layer.

A standard Token-2022 Transfer Hook primarily determines whether a transfer is allowed. Bordrless’s own Token Standard allows Hooks to define rules around fees, revenue distribution, burns, holder rewards, and holding-time-based mechanisms. The DEX also invokes these Hooks during trading, while the launchpad is part of the same system.

This means developers could theoretically design different tokenomics directly into their tokens, rather than relying entirely on external bots to execute buybacks, distributions, or burns. BORDR’s long-term potential lies in whether broader adoption could turn Bordrless from a launchpad into foundational infrastructure for programmable token economics on Solana.

There are two main recent catalysts.

Product modules are progressively going live. The website showcases components including the Token Standard, DEX, launchpad, bridge, and SDK. The team has also announced the launch of AI Studio and previewed upcoming features such as Hook Studio and Companions.

The developer ecosystem is taking shape. Open-source programs and SDKs lower the barrier to entry. The market is not simply betting on an individual token, but on the possibility that developers will use this infrastructure to create tokens with differentiated economic rules.

Together, these developments have encouraged the market to price in the possibility that Bordrless could become an infrastructure layer for a new generation of programmable tokens on Solana.

Fundamentals have improved, but mainly in terms of product maturity and the strength of the ecosystem narrative. Actual adoption remains at an early stage.

The website currently shows 21 launches and zero graduated projects, with approximately $110K in 24-hour trading volume, $26.8K in pool liquidity, and $1.12K in creator fees.

These figures show that the product is no longer purely conceptual, but they do not yet demonstrate that it can attract a large number of projects with sustained usage. In particular, the lack of graduated projects means long-term retention, successful launch case studies, and post-graduation trading depth still need to be proven.

BORDR’s price has also risen significantly, but the entire move cannot be attributed to any single product update. A more reasonable interpretation is that product development, developer tools, trading access, and KOL coverage have collectively strengthened market expectations. Determining the contribution of each factor would require a closer look at transaction-level data and the timeline of events.

Going forward, I will focus on three variables:

1. Hook Studio goes fully live. If developers can easily design, deploy, and share custom Hooks, Bordrless could evolve from a collection of in-house products into a broader developer platform.

2. Companions generates real usage. The team has described a mechanism through which creator fees flow into on-chain programs and are allocated according to predefined rules for buybacks, burns, holder distributions, or other purposes. If multiple projects generate meaningful trading activity through this system, that would be much stronger evidence than simply adding more features.

3. External projects adopt the standard consistently. The real inflection point is not another module going live. It is independent developers choosing to issue tokens using the standard and generating sustained trading volume, fees, and user demand.

There are two major risks.

First, product complexity may be running ahead of demand. Programmable tokens offer considerable technical flexibility, but ordinary issuers may not need such complex mechanisms. Without sufficient developer adoption, even a fully developed product may struggle to generate network effects.

Second, BORDR’s value capture has not been sufficiently established. Even if the Bordrless DEX, launchpad, and SDK grow, that does not mean all of this growth will translate into buying demand for BORDR. Its specific utility, revenue distribution model, and ability to generate sustained token demand still need to be verified.

Security is another consideration. The website states that the relevant programs retain upgrade authority pending completion of audits. For infrastructure responsible for token rules, fee distribution, and burns, this is a risk that deserves continued monitoring.

My conclusion is that the most meaningful change behind BORDR’s recent rally is its transition from the concept of a new Token Standard toward an infrastructure project with code, product modules, and developer tools. The market is betting on whether it can become a foundational layer for programmable token economics on Solana.

What will determine whether its valuation can expand further is not another explanation of how advanced Hooks are, but whether developer adoption, real trading activity, and BORDR’s value capture can grow together.

The fundamentals are moving in the right direction, but ecosystem scale and token value capture remain at an early stage.

text:
A user could create a subscription that the system could never charge, change, or cleanly remove.

A review Zealynx co-audited with Shieldify exposed the identity split behind that dead end in Bastion Wallet.

An EOA could register directly through `Initiator`, bypassing the expected `SubExecutor` entry path. The subscription was then stored under the EOA, while later operations looked for it under the SubExecutor.

Payment failed a second way: the recorded initiator and the caller expected by `processPayment()` no longer matched.

The High-severity finding was fixed by restricting those operations to `SubExecutor` and moving the core validation into `Initiator`.
author: ZealynxSecurity

text:
The intended lifecycle was one connected path: `SubExecutor.createSubscription()` → registration → payment initiation → `SubExecutor.processPayment()`.

The direct call skipped the first identity boundary, so every later step inherited inconsistent state.

text:
Palantir 的那块「监控全世界」的情报大屏，现在已经有人在 GitHub 上做成免费版了。

刚看到一个叫 Osiris 的开源项目，挺有意思。

打开网站就是一颗 3D 地球，你可以把全球民航、部分可公开追踪的军机、卫星、公共摄像头、地震、NASA 监测的火灾热点、核设施和冲突地区全部叠在地图上。

项目号称接入了超过 1.7 万个公共摄像头，还整合了 DNS、WHOIS、IP 情报、漏洞查询，甚至可以追踪 BTC、ETH 钱包地址，查询美国 OFAC 制裁名单。

现在作者还加了 AI 助手，允许你接入自己的模型 API Key，直接对着地图提问、查询情报，甚至尝试预测事件走向。

我去翻了下 GitHub，已经超过 1 万 Star，MIT 开源协议。

有意思的是，这些数据其实大多早就公开了，来自 OpenSky、NASA、USGS 以及各地的交通部门。过去散落在几十个网站和数据库里的信息，现在被装进了同一张地图，视觉效果相当震撼。

当然，把它叫作「开源 Palantir」多少有点碰瓷。

Osiris 的部分冲突地区信息仍然是静态标注，网络扫描功能也需要额外配置后端。Palantir 真正昂贵的地方，是深入政府和企业内部，把私有数据、实体关系、权限管理和实际业务决策连接起来。这些能力远没有那么容易复制。

但我还是很喜欢这种项目。

过去我们看到情报机构使用这种全球态势监控系统，总觉得背后有什么了不起的黑科技。现在回头看，至少在公开情报这个领域，很多东西已经没有那么神秘了。

而且我觉得随着 AI Agent 的发展，这类产品还有很大空间。把几万个数据点放在地图上已经不难，接下来更有价值的，是让 AI 自己寻找不同信息之间的关联，从中发现人类没有注意到的异常。

毕竟看到一架飞机从地图上飞过去，和知道这架飞机为什么值得关注，中间还差着很远。

项目地址和在线体验我放到评论区👇

I feel like everyone is going to figure out at the same time (in 1-4 months or so) that our biggest problem today with AI isn’t actually an AI problem. 

The problem is we’re not giving our AIs clear enough definitions of what we want. 

So our AIs basically go off and build in some direction, but not exactly the direction you want to go in. 

This problem has three main parts:

1. You knowing what you want 

2. You being able to articulate that thing thoroughly and accurately 

3. Your AI being able to do that thing

Everyone assumes the problem is with number 3, but it’s usually a combination of 1 and 2.

The next biggest advancement in AI (or one of them anyway) is going to come from harnesses building this concept of ideal state, evals, and hill-climbing directly into their DNA. 

In the model providers can help as well by eliciting this from the user and building this before any work is done. 

Ideal State, Evals, and hill-climbing. This is where it’s at.

这条推文的建议很好，但"把压缩调到 400K"对每个人都成立吗？不一定。

这就是 magpie 要做本地 agent 可观测性分析的原因。每个 agent 都有自己独特的行为，每个用户也有自己的使用习惯，任务难度也因人而异，所以不存在一份对所有人都最优的配置。

更麻烦的是，每个 agent 的配置项又多又复杂，还藏得很深。大多数人压根儿不知道有这些开关，就这么不知不觉地用着最不适合自己的配置，浪费了大量时间和 Token，甚至牺牲了完成任务的质量。

magpie 新功能「为你调优」：在本地用你自己的真实调用，按每个 agent、每个模型去回放压缩阈值和缓存时长，算出对你最省 Token 的那一组。千人千面，但对每个人都是最省的。

quoted_text:
最近用 Claude Code 跑长任务经常感觉 5 小时额度像流水一样掉？之前社区甚至有人吐槽它根本没做上下文压缩，暗地里疯狂塞 token。今天看了 Anthropic 官方工程师 Lydia Hallie 的详细解释，才发现大家都误解了它的机制，实际问题出在默认策略太激进。

很多人不知道，auto-compact 其实是真正在做摘要的。只要一触发，前面所有的历史记录都会被一段很短的 summary 直接替换掉，根本不会在上下文里保留上百万的冗余内容。

那为什么大家的配额还是崩得飞快？ 关键在于 1M 上下文模型下，系统默认一定要憋到将近 967K 才会启动自动压缩。这就很要命了——在憋到 967K 之前的那段漫长对话里，你发过去的每一句话，背后都在默默拖着七八百 K 甚至近百万 token 的庞大上下文。即便大部分命中了 Prompt Cache 且读取单价很低，但只要基数膨胀到这个量级，每一轮对话依然在疯狂蚕食你的 5 小时用量。
还有人纠结“压缩会导致前缀改变、缓存失效，重新写一遍岂不是血亏”。其实完全不会。生成摘要本身走的大多是热缓存读取，失效之后你只需要为那段极短的新摘要付一次小额的 Cache Write，换来的却是后续交互基数直接腰斩，长远来看绝对是划算的。

不想额度莫名其妙被吞完的话，建议赶紧顺手做两个调整：

平时在终端直接敲个 /autocompact 400k，或者在 ~/.claude/settings.json 里配置好 autoCompactWindow，强制它提前压缩，别让上下文滚雪球滚到 900多K。

另外个人订阅的缓存保活时间默认是 1 小时，但后台子代理（subagent）只有 5 分钟。如果写代码停顿久了，缓存冷掉重写确实心疼，有需要可以在配置里改一下 promptCacheTtl 和 subagentPromptCacheTtl。如果主会话跑的是 Opus，顺便把后台打杂的 subagent 换成更轻量的模型，额度立马耐用很多

text:
The Copernican Model

Over the last few months, I’ve been studying the crypto models that seem to be discussed on a "fundamentals" basis: HYPE/Aave/Venice/etc, following the users/ revenue/relationship between a useful product and its token - all to create a sort of "value accural ontology." This is a case study from that research.

The reason was more selfish: I wanted to understand which models work when your business has to interact with the "real world," namely for how we want to take  @usdai_official for the most alignemnt

As a founder, I’ve had doors literally shut on my face when we started because we’re “crypto” (literally left in the waiting room like a tv show). I still believe tokenization is one of the most important technologies we have today. But the institutions we need to work with often want a equity counterparty, a board, and a contract. You just wont get around this for the next 10 years (no a cayman foundation doesnt work)

That experience has made me increasingly interested in the role of an equity surrogate: an independent operating business that connects a network to the world outside it.. but frankly there werent many clean examples out there without value destruction. 

The case I keep returning to is @tradexyz and Hyperliquid.. and im not really sure they even know how symbiotic of a relationship they created. They technically SHOULD be the same team.. but they are divided across the river due to regulatory issues, while being symbiotic

Consider the S&P 500 agreement, they licensed the benchmark to tradexyz for a perpetual market: the institutional relationship sits with the company, but the product runs on the network.

tradexyz can negotiate licenses, develop products, operate markets, and build distribution. Hyperliquid provides shared execution and settlement infrastructure. 

And if theres a company that ever wants "exposure" to the Hyperliquid business, but they just cant buy a "token" (and believe me, it's super super hard to get a traditional enterprise to buy a token, it doesnt fucking matter if you have an ETF, you literally have to convince a boomer board to do it and get the infrastructure set up to do it). Instaed, they could just invest in this equity, as it is not burning the HYPE it buys, but is increasing its share of it. so instead of buyback-n-burn, its closer to commit-n-compound.  

I’ve started thinking about this as a value-accrual architecture, with two different forms of capital (terms best described by a16z crypto's post in 2025):

Network asset: scarcity at the core.

- Its supply discipline can become more credible, its economics more programmatic, and its operation less dependent on any single company. 
- It coordinates shared infrastructure and connects activity across many businesses to a common asset.
- That is what I mean by a progressively hardening asset. The scarcity and independence have to be earned through the design of the system.
- Not capital intensive, as it must be smart contract based.
- Can often place be the seat of the "decentralized security" - as there is no central underwriter. If HYPE was a company.. itd be regulated out of the wazoo.

Enterprise equity: elasticity at the edge.

- A company can issue shares, raise capital, hire people, acquire licenses, and build products. 
- Its capital structure can expand with the work required to bring the network into the real world.
- New shares dilute ownership percentages, but productive investment can increase value per share. 
- That ability to finance expansion is why I think of equity as elastic
- This is the part where its OK to be regulated, because most of the regulational burden is held by HYPE, theyre just asset issuers.

These different traits are the reason to combine them.

An enterprise can raise the capital to grow while the network maintains its own supply discipline. The connection is the activity that expansion creates, and the mechanisms that route value from that activity back to the network.

Hyperliquid makes part of that relationship explicit. Trading generates fees for the deployer and the protocol. The Assistance Fund (insurance) automatically converts its allocated fees into HYPE, which the documentation specifies is burned. Hyperliquid fee mechanics

The broader strategy I take from this is Commit & Compound that is conducted around the equity enterprise. It's effectively what a DAT 2.0 would do: create a business first, then max-bid HYPE with that entity, then get new investors to invest in the convexity of HYPE^2.

Build a useful business around the network. Commit capital to its asset. Retain exposure to the infrastructure your business helps make more valuable.

For a company that accumulates and holds the network asset, growing enterprise value and participating in network value become connected opportunities. There is a business to capitalize and a shared ecosystem in which to hold an economic stake.

That is why I find the assumption that every successful application eventually needs its own token less compelling. Building a valuable company around an existing network asset is a meaningful strategy in its own right.

Notice how much kinetic language I’m using: commitment, circulation, gravity

I think network assets and enterprise assets represent different forms of gravity

HYPE is the sun: the network asset at the center

tradexyz equity is a planet: an enterprise building its business around that network

Its real-world integrations are moons: the licenses, institutional relationships, and distribution channels that gather around the enterprise and extend its reach

Enterprise value forms around network value. Real-world relationships form around enterprise value. Their activity feeds back into the shared system.

Personally, I think the greatest value can ultimately accrue at the network level. But that belief has to be substantiated by the businesses being built around it: real users, useful products, liquidity, and recurring economic activity.

A token doesn’t acquire gravity simply because we call it a network asset.

This is the distinction I found useful in a16z’s writing: can the network function and accrue value independently of the original company? Can other businesses build on it and contribute to its economics? 

The company can become a great business. The network can become the foundation for many great businesses.

Scarcity at the core. Productive expansion around it.

I’ve learned a lot from this Commit & Compound structure, with a Copernican asset at the center.

It has changed how I’m thinking about USDAI and CHIP. More on that in the next post

quoted_text:
REA：让 AI 智能体帮你逆向没有源码的软件

开源项目 REA（Reverse Engineer Anything）把逆向分析工具接到了 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类 AI 编程智能体上。看到别人 App 里有个好功能，可以让智能体去拆这个程序，讲清楚功能是怎么实现的，附上证据，再在你自己的项目里写一个类似的。逆向分析指的是手里没有源代码，从编译好的程序反推它是怎么写的。

REA 本身是一个 MCP 服务。MCP 是 AI 智能体调用外部工具的通用接口，接上以后，智能体在对话里就能直接调用 REA 的分析功能。安装只需一行命令 npx rea-agents setup，它会注册到 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI、Grok Build 等智能体里，改配置前会先备份并让你确认。不用智能体的话，也可以在终端里直接跑命令。

能分析的东西很多。原生程序（直接编译成机器码的软件）要借助 Hopper、Ghidra 或 IDA 这几款反汇编工具，把机器码还原成汇编和近似 C 语言的伪代码。Electron 应用（用网页技术做的桌面软件，比如 Notion）可以直接拆开安装包里的 ASAR 归档文件，理清模块和进程间通信，不需要额外工具。此外还支持 .NET 程序、安卓 APK、固件、网站、抓包记录、以太坊合约字节码，以及在 Linux 和 macOS 上记录程序运行时的行为。

分析在本机进行，REA 不上传目标程序，但分析结果会交给智能体背后的模型服务商，数据怎么处理看各家政策。

项目给了三个案例。一是经典打砖块游戏 DX-Ball：从一次播放音效的调用，追到根据球的位置计算左右声道的函数，把不完整的伪代码还原成 C 代码，3205 组测试结果和原版一致，编译出的 63 个字节也和原版完全相同。二是 Notion 桌面版：追踪复制粘贴从界面一路经过预加载脚本、进程间通信到主进程的完整链路。三是日本老电脑 PC-98 上的游戏《东方幻想乡》（TH04）：从 16 位指令里还原出弹幕子弹环的角度算法。

对安全研究员、做老游戏复刻和软件保存的人来说，以前要自己对着反汇编工具一行行读、一层层追调用，现在可以让智能体先追，人来核对它给出的证据。普通开发者想研究竞品某个功能的做法，也多了一条路。

README 显示项目在 GitHub 上已有 5 万星。npm 包今年 7 月首次发布，最新的 6.3.0 版今天刚发。

使用前注意两点。项目声明只支持合法的逆向研究，授权和合规由使用者自己负责，逆向别人的软件可能违反用户协议或版权法规。项目还说明从未发行或背书任何加密货币，借用 REA 名字的代币都与它无关。

text:
The more agents and projects you have running, the harder it gets to keep track of everything through chat alone.

This is where Hermes Kanban comes in.

Here's how Hermes Kanban works, why it's worth using, and how I'd recommend setting it up:

Chat is where you work with an agent.
Kanban is where you manage the work across agents.

Hermes Kanban gives you a visual dashboard for tracking tasks across your agents and projects. But it's much more than a task board.

Here's what you can do with it:

• Create tasks and assign them to specific Hermes agents.
• Track what's ready, running, blocked, or completed.
• Set dependencies so tasks wait for other work to finish.
• Coordinate handoffs between specialized agents.
• Review progress and see where something needs your attention.

And with the dispatcher, Hermes can pick up tasks that are ready to run and launch the appropriate agent to handle them.

Now, here's something I'd recommend:

**Create a separate Kanban board for each major project.**

For example:

📌 Content production
Research → Drafting → Review → Assets → Done

📌 Software development
Bugs → Features → Testing → Review → Done

📌 Business operations
Research → Waiting → In Progress → Blocked → Done

Hermes supports multiple isolated boards, so each project can have its own tasks, workspaces, logs, and agent workflows. You can also connect a board to a Hermes Project to keep the work tied to the right project context.

The more work you hand off to Hermes, the more valuable this becomes.

Instead of digging through conversations trying to figure out what every agent is doing, give each project its own board and manage the work from one place.

quoted_text:
papertrade launch timing and details

papertrade is expected to launch at 14:00 UTC on 10.10.2026, following the scheduled hyperevm network upgrade. 

at this time trading through the frontend will be enabled.

deposits will pause for a short period of time at 13:45 UTC, fifteen minutes before, to ensure that trading has the utmost priority during launch. if you wish to participate in the launch you must predeposit.

launch congestion

papertrade will be congested at the start due to launch demand. expect temporarily long confirmation wait times, especially for smaller notional trades. 

the frontend relayer plays an important role during launch, controlling how transactions are submitted to the hyperevm. some actions like staking distributions run separately in big blocks. the chain will always look as if only half of all possible gas is being used, this is optimal. using more than this would exponentially raise fees within minutes to unpayable prices.

oi limits

papertrade has individual atomic position limits of 10m. there is no limit on the number of 10m positions a user can have. papertrade also has floating oi headroom per market/side, which determines how much oi can be opened in a very short period. these are not designed to be triggered through normal trading usage and are set at 1bn per market/side for launch.

asym pnl fee parameters

papertrade inherits rollbit’s asymmetric fee pnl curve 

the parameters are:
-baseRate: .1
-rateMultiplier: 15000
-rateExponent: 1
-referenceNotional: 100000*k (k=1m)
-positionMultiplier: 814.598 btc / 483.979 eth
-profit deadman: 0.2 basis points

a visualization of the pnl parameter curve is below

admin keys

the papertrade admins (2 of 3 multisigs consisting of @izebel_eth @blurr @UngusTrade ) perform three separate roles: 

-guardian: pause opens and freeze individual/global markets. if a market is frozen any existing positions can still be closed against the paused bbo mid.

-owner: set impact curve and fee parameters. change configure relayers/keepers. list new markets and upgrade the contracts. all contract upgrades are gated by a 7 day timelock.

-markets: adjust the oi headroom per market/side. set the minimum margin and minimum position sizes.

read more about these features at: https://t.co/TTCuHgCHpB

text:
Here’s essentially the expansion board broken down. It’s got two PCIE switches inside, meaning that you only need a singular x16 slot to power 8 GPUs (or two). 

Let’s talk about how it works. 

First, the main 8 GPUs slots

You have two methods of setup here:
- Direct connect via two PCIE x16 -> 4x x8 MCIO
- Cascade via a single PCIE x16 -> 2x x8 MCIO

The difference here is how much of your GPU usage do you want heading back to your CPU vs keeping everyone around one dimension for faster GPU -> GPU communication. 

A quick way to think about it: model fits on 8 GPUs? Cascade. CPU offload? Probably direct connect. 

But what IS cascade?

Let’s look back at the diagram. 

Direct connect says that we’re going to plug in two slots worth of x8 connectors into both 0-7 and 8-15 slots (two halves of our PCIE x16) into the separate halves. This then populates the switch in such a way that we can support 8 GPUs, each on separate 4-GPU P2P groupings. 

The nice part here is because the PCIE switches live in this board, you can take four additional MCIO cables and go from the output downlink into any one of the direct connect interfaces and add an additional GPU. 

BUT, if you want the two groups of 4 GPUs to interact, they’ll get tunneled through a single x16 slot worth of transfer, and have to go through the CPU. Not a fun bottleneck when dealing with 64 lanes worth of GPUs on either side. 

The alternative is what we call “cascade.” 

If we don’t want to worry about the CPU side (e.g. model inference), we can instead only hook up one PCIE slot as the input, then take the downlink from SW1 and use it as the INPUT to SW2. 

It’s still the bandwidth of a singular PCIE5 x16 slot, but you avoid going through the CPU which saves you some cycles. 

For the full 12 GPUs, you would need 3-4 full x16 slots on your motherboard. With the direct connect slots running through the host CPU still (since they are direct connect), if you’re not doing cascading. 

Or translation: 
- Non-DC: slot 1 and slot 12 are powered through additional retimers and MCIO at x16 and don’t add a slot, it’s just moving your existing PCIE slots somewhere else. Then you power slots 2 and 11 through the “jump” mentioned earlier
- DC: slot 1, 12, and then 2 or 11 are powered through a retimer, and then the other (between 2 and 11) are powered through the “jump”

Now let’s get into how I plan to use this. 

I have 9 GPUs in total (8 6000’s and a 6000 ADA), so I’ll be doing the Cascade, then using the SW2 output to power a 9th PCIE slot similar to the non-Cascade version that could power 10. 

What I don’t know yet is which is better: TP4/PP2, or TP8 over the two P2P groups, but I expect that would be the difference of batching. I’ll probably accept some slowness and do TP8. I can’t predict how much slower that will be, so when it comes in I’ll do these full benchmarks in many different combinations. 

What I want you to gather from this is these boards have internal PCIE switches, to help avoid needing to go through the CPU to have your GPUs interact, and bring you a larger lane budget than your CPU would allow.

so about the $86m ledger drain. everyone’s screaming “ledger got hacked” again. i spent the evening digging and it’s dumber and scarier than that

there’s a shop in malaysia called cryptobilis that sells hardware wallets. ledger has it listed as an official authorized reseller since at least 2022, for malaysia, indonesia and the philippines. legit shop, real devices, years of normal customers

this spring the founders sell it. the deal comes with an NDA: they can’t tell anyone about the sale until october 19

by august the company registry shows one owner with 100%. some guy from heilongjiang, china

the shop keeps running like nothing happened. the site, the name and the “authorized by ledger” badge all stay up

then on oct 8 @MagicalTux posts photos of a ledger he cracked open. hidden under the screen there’s an extra little board with an LTE modem and an eSIM. it just watches the display. you set up your wallet, your 24 words show up, and they get sent out over mobile data. ledger’s genuine check doesn’t catch it because the actual ledger chip is real. his device came from malaysia

https://t.co/vRuBM0xIfR

that post does 120k views

22 hours later someone sweeps everything. 203 BTC hits two addresses in literally one block. ~$58m USDT moves on tron in the same hour. i added up all the wallets: ~$91m

about 7 hours after that ledger says “we’re investigating” and asks cryptobilis to pause sales

cryptobilis is still on ledger’s site as an authorized reseller

to be fair, nobody has officially tied the new owner to the bugged devices yet, and ledger hasn’t confirmed how it happened. but read it as a business plan:

get authorized, sell real stuff for years, quietly sell the company under an NDA, keep the badge, ship devices that phone home, then drain everything the second someone notices

and was ledger even told the shop got sold? nobody’s said so

“authorized reseller” means ledger trusted whoever ran the shop back in 2022. says nothing about who runs it today

bought your hardware wallet anywhere but the manufacturer? open it up today, ledger literally has a guide for that. then move to a fresh seed on a device bought direct

wonder who’s going to answer for this: the chinese frontman from heilongjiang, the shop’s previous owners, or ledger itself

@Ledger clearly needs to keep a much closer eye on who they call official resellers, and take way more responsibility for who sells their devices and how

author: star_okx
quoted_text:
No complexity. No accident.
10/10 was caused by irresponsible marketing campaigns by certain companies.

On October 10, tens of billions of dollars were liquidated. As CEO of OKX, we observed clearly that the crypto market’s microstructure fundamentally changed after that day.

Many industry participants believe the damage was more severe than the FTX collapse. Since then, there has been extensive discussion about why it happened and how to prevent a recurrence. The root causes are not difficult to identify.

⸻

What actually happened
1.Binance launched a temporary user-acquisition campaign offering 12% APY on USDe, while allowing USDe to be used as collateral with the same treatment as USDT and USDC, and without effective limits.
2.USDe is a tokenized hedge fund product.
Ethena raises capital via a so-called “stablecoin,” deploys it into index arbitrage and algorithmic trading strategies, and tokenizes the resulting fund. The token can then be deposited on exchanges to earn yield.
3.USDe is fundamentally different from products such as
BlackRock BUIDL and Franklin Templeton BENJI, which are tokenized money market funds with low-risk profiles.
USDe, by contrast, embeds hedge-fund-level risk. This difference is structural, not cosmetic.
4.Binance users were encouraged to convert USDT and USDC into USDe to earn attractive yields, without sufficient emphasis on the underlying risks. From a user’s perspective, trading with USDe appeared no different from trading with traditional stablecoins—while the actual risk profile was materially higher.
5.Risk escalated further as users:
•converted USDT/USDC into USDe,
•used USDe as collateral to borrow USDT,
•converted the borrowed USDT back into USDe,
•and repeated the cycle.
This leverage loop produced artificial APYs of 24%, 36%, and even 70%+, widely perceived as “low risk” simply because they were offered by a major platform. Systemic risk accumulated rapidly across the global crypto market.
https://t.co/IK2gW4xUOP that point, even a small market shock was sufficient to trigger a collapse.
When volatility hit, USDe depegged quickly. Cascading liquidations followed, and weaknesses in risk management around assets such as WETH and BNSOL further amplified the crash. Some tokens briefly traded near zero.
The damage to global users and companies—including OKX customers—was severe, and recovery will take time.

⸻

Why this matters

I am discussing the root cause, not assigning blame or launching an attack on Binance. Speaking openly about systemic risks is sometimes uncomfortable, but it is necessary if the industry is to mature responsibly. 

I expect there may be significant misinformation and coordinated FUD directed at OKX in the near future. Even so, speaking honestly about systemic risk is the right thing to do—and we will continue to do so.

As the largest global platform, Binance has outsized influence—and corresponding responsibility—as an industry leader. Long-term trust in crypto cannot be built on short-term yield games, excessive leverage, or marketing practices that obscure risk.

The industry needs leaders who prioritize market stability, transparency, and responsible innovation—not a winner-take-all mentality where criticism is treated as hostility.

Crypto is still early.
What we choose to normalize today will determine whether this industry earns lasting trust—or repeats the same mistakes again.

text:
写给对「OpenETF 会怎么做产品」好奇的朋友。

我们要回答的问题是：在一张空白画布上，如何负责任地设计一个可长期发展的产品。

OpenETF 的设计难在三件事。

第一，从零搭一个新的链上金融原语：fully onchain funds，也就是我们说的 ETF。

链上基金不缺参照：Hyperliquid 的旧版金库、传统基金、交易所交易基金。但地基换成 HyperCore 和 HyperEVM 之后，很多前提都变了。哪些可以借鉴，哪些要重新想，我们需要更第一性的思考，think long term，think scalable，think big。

第二，我们需要清晰觉察、审慎对待我们所拥有的潜在权力和影响力：OpenETF 会处在一个对信息、注意力和资金流向都有优势的位置。

基金管理人、投资人、合作方和我们之间是多边关系，会发生什么样的动态关系和化学反应，是我们做设计时一直在思考的要素。

第三，也是最重要的，里面涉及的会是大量资金，而且是别人托付的钱。

哪些地方可以交给链上去验证，哪些地方仍然需要信任，信任又该落在谁身上、怎么被看见，每一处都要想清楚。能不靠信任的地方，就尽量不靠信任；剩下的部分，需要我们用严谨和专业去对待。

——

一个产品是很多小决定的总和，方向取决于团队把什么当作根本。这篇写下的七条不是随手列的要素，它们会引领产品的生长。每一句都斟酌良久，代表了 OpenETF 的产品价值观。

DMs open，欢迎基金管理人一起交流。

quoted_text:
最近和几个审查方案的同事聊天，感觉大家心里都窝着一股气，还不太好发。

现在有些新人交上来的方案，写得相当牛逼。技术先进，思路完整，各种术语信手拈来。一看就知道用了 AI，再聊两句，也能发现，里面不少内容已经超出了他自己的理解。

但方案交上来了，总得有人审。

审查人员就得一段一段看，查依据、找漏洞，判断这些技术到底适不适合当前项目。越是写得像那么回事，越不能随便放过去。有些地方读着很顺，仔细琢磨才发现不对，光把问题说明白就得费半天劲。

审完以后，把新人叫过来，一条条讲。他也挺配合，认真记下来，回去喂给 AI，很快又交上来一篇。

然后你接着审。

上一轮的问题改没改对，这一轮又有没有冒出新问题，都得重新看。对方改稿挺快，你却没法跟着快。几轮下来，方案越来越漂亮，审的人脑仁疼。

你花了大量精力审一篇文章，可能比对方生成它花的精力还多。好不容易把问题理清楚了，送回去，过一会儿又端上来一盘。至于他到底有没有理解你说的问题，还得再问。

可你也不好直接批评新人。你不让他用 AI，他自己写的可能更烂；你让他自己先审，他又真审不出来。里面有些技术，他以前都没接触过，现在第一次见，就是出现在自己署名的方案里。

这事让我越来越觉得棘手。以前新人写方案，水平有限，问题也往往比较直白。现在 AI 帮他把方案拔高了，审查的难度也跟着拔高了，但他本人未必能跟上。我隐约觉得这是以后的一个大问题。

text:
截止到今天，加密市场市值排行前300的代币里，只有10个左右还站在去年10月10日高点之上。

去年10月是整个加密市场的高点。一年过去，绝大多数币都还在那波高点的阴影里，只有这些相对抗跌甚至创新高，它们相较于去年10月的涨幅分别是：

1 Zcash（ $ZEC ）+392.2%

隐私币龙头。今年隐私叙事重新抬头，加上 ETF 资金流入和交易所流动性改善，成了整个市场里表现最强的大盘币之一。

2 JUST（ just:native）+336.3%

TRON 生态的 DeFi 套件治理代币，核心产品包括 JustLend 借贷和之前的 JustStable 稳定币体系。业务实用，叙事相对传统，更多是靠 TRON 生态的稳定使用量和治理价值。

3 Quant（ $QNT ）+149.2%

做区块链互操作性的企业级中间层，让不同公链、私链和传统金融系统能互相通信。
今年被美国清算机构选中做代币化存款相关基础设施后，叙事从“一直在做的事”变成了“真正有大客户落地”。

4 Hyperliquid（$HYPE）+95.3%
无需多言，真实收入和代币回购驱动。

5 NEAR Protocol（$NEAR）+65.9%
高性能 L1，现在主打 AI Agent 和 Chain Abstraction。在往“用户拥有的 AI”和链上 Agent 经济靠，同时有一定隐私相关特性。

6 Monero（$XMR）+60.1%
真正默认隐私的数字现金，环签名 + 隐身地址，交易不可追踪。被多家交易所下架后反而更凸显它的“不可审查”属性，在隐私币赛道里一直是 ZEC 的情绪外溢。

7 Morpho（$MORPHO）+48.8%
Coinbase、Robinhood 等平台都在用它做借贷/收益产品，属于真正在给大机构提供底层信用基础设施的 DeFi。

8 Sky（$SKY）+16.8%
原 MakerDAO，现在的稳定币发行方（DAI / USDS）。治理代币从 MKR 迁移到 SKY，核心业务还是超额抵押的去中心化稳定币 + 储蓄利率，DeFi 里老牌的“美元打印机”。

9 Dash（$DASH）+10.4%
老牌数字现金，有 InstantSend 和可选隐私功能（PrivateSend），靠主节点网络支撑。叙事已经很老了，但作为隐私叙事外溢还能勉强站在高点之上。

10 链上黄金：Tether Gold（$XAUT）+2.2%、PAX Gold（$PAXG）+2.1%、Kinesis Gold +1.5%，本质上是跟着实物黄金走，不太算加密原生叙事。

一年过去，还能回来的基本就剩隐私、企业级互操作、真实收入驱动的 DEX、AI 基础设施和老牌 DeFi 这几条线了。

Grok bot和Muse邪修大法：

1. 装 Pi Agent，重活丢给第三方免费模型  
在 Muse 里装 Pi Agent，模型走蚂蚁百灵 Ling 这类开放平台免费额度（每天约 50 万 token）。长文、写代码、批处理走外部免费模型，Muse 自己的周额度留给必须用 Muse Spark 的步骤。

2. 监控 Cloudflare 用量，防止账单爆炸  
Worker 免费档大约每天 10 万请求，家宽链式、中继、归档一旦被扫或被 Bot 轮询，很容易打穿。让 Agent 用官方模板建只读用量查询，设日请求和 CPU 时间阈值，超了就告警。

3. Muse Video 做竖屏素材，人审后再发小红书  
免费额度每周大约能出 20–30 条，加上邀请额度非常够用。适合脚本、分镜、口播底片。

4. 搭配落地 IP 跑 Claude Code

5. 搭配回国代理，做闲鱼管家  

6. 用 Tailscale 对 Muse、Grok Bot、家里机器组网 
Muse 有原生 Tailscale 连接器。组网后用 MagicDNS 互访，重活放家里或已有 VPS 上，Muse 做编排。

7. Cookie 同步解决云浏览器的登录墙  
本机扩展导出已登录站点的 session cookie，同步进 Bot/Muse 的 Chrome，实现无密码登录。

8. 把 Muse 额度接到 Grok Bot
用 muse2api 让 Grok Bot 消耗 Muse 的 token 写代码、生图、生视频。

9. 定时任务
Muse 用 Scheduled Tasks / Goals，Grok Bot 用 Routine。

10. Grok 多 Bot 分工，Muse 做生活管家
Grok 适合养收件、写代码、运营多个 Bot，共用一台云电脑的文件和登录态。Muse 用于邮件、日历、采购这类生活流程。
